chunks: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asked me, 'What do you ride?' I said, 'A donkey.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'For how much did you buy it?' I said, 'For thirteen dinars.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'This is extravagance — to buy a donkey for thirteen dinars and neglect a work-horse.' I said, 'My Master, the upkeep of a work-horse is more than the upkeep of a donkey.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The One Who provides for the donkey will provide for the work-horse. Do you not know that whoever keeps an animal in expectation of our matter (the Rising of al-Qa'im), by which he provokes our enemy, and he is affiliated with us — Allah will make his livelihood flow abundantly, open his chest, fulfill his aspirations, and it will be an aid for his needs.'

key_terms.أَمْرَنَا: our matter — refers to the awaited Rising (qiyam) of Imam al-Qa'im, the twelfth Imam
key_terms.السَّرَفُ: extravagance (israf) — wasting resources on lesser things when better options are available
key_terms.الْبِرْذَوْن: work-horse (birdhawn) — a horse used for riding and service, considered more dignified than a donkey
key_terms.مَنْسُوبٌ إِلَيْنَا: affiliated with us — one who is a devotee and supporter of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim say about keeping a horse for the cause of Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kazim (AS) corrects Ibn Tayfur al-Mutatabib's choice to ride a donkey over a work-horse, calling it extravagance (israf). When Ibn Tayfur objects that a horse costs more to maintain, the Imam reassures him that God who provides for a donkey will also provide for a horse. The deeper teaching is that keeping a noble animal in anticipation of the Imam's cause brings divine blessings: abundant livelihood, spiritual expansion, and fulfillment of needs. This hadith reflects the Shia tradition of material and spiritual preparation for the eventual uprising (qiyam) of the awaited Imam al-Qa'im, and teaches that sincere alignment with the Ahlulbayt transforms even worldly decisions into acts of devotion.
